items.title: Dalton Richards Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: Miss Neda St. Paul, that was George St. Paul's daughter before she married. All her little cocktail parties she used to give on Phillip Street there. We played a couple of houses over there, too.

ctx.x: He's a piano player. No, not here. He's a brother.

No, no. Man, that guy was a saxophone player, a supreme. I mean, he, he gave the incentive to play. And I used to like to hire him. And sometimes I'd use, uh, Son Johnson, that's George Johnson, and Parnell together. Well, that's two of the best saxophone players in the city, see? And we had Al, Alvin Alcon, and Alvin French singing, and had a little fella called Jim Davis on the bass. But we had, I always did bring up there, a good outfit for those boys, and they were very well pleased, you see? And, uh, during…

By the way, Alvin Alcorn is working with that group now again. Yeah, he is. They don't have Fernandes anymore. No. Albert's finances quit? Well, I don't know. There's some, maybe a disagreement or something, and so they're using Alvin at present. Well, I tell you. For some time now, a few weeks or months at least, here.
